question_text: Transform the equation √3x+y=4 into (i) slope intercept form (ii) intercept form.

recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this — say what each of the two forms must look like when you are finished.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Slope intercept form
steps.margin_note: First mark. Slope-intercept form is y = mx + c, so make y the subject and read off the slope and the y-intercept.
lines: (i) Slope intercept form is  y = mx + c

recall.must_convey: That the equation is rearranged into y = mx + c.
accept: make y the subject to get y equals m x plus c
divide through so y is alone
slope intercept form is y equals m x plus c
heard_as: y equals m x plus c

steps.why: Slope-intercept form shows the slope and the y-intercept directly, which is what makes it the form asked for first.
common_mistakes: Leaving the equation with y on the wrong side.
Dividing only some terms by the coefficient of y.

steps.label: Intercept form
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Intercept form is x/a + y/b = 1, so move the constant to the right and divide everything by it — the two denominators are then the intercepts.

recall.must_convey: That moving the constant across and dividing gives x/(4/√3) + y/4 = 1.
accept: move the constant to the right and divide everything by it
intercept form is x over a plus y over b equals one
divide through by the constant to get one on the right
constant ni right side ki teesi divide cheyyali

steps.why: Intercept form must have 1 on the right-hand side — that is the whole definition, and dividing by the constant is the only way to arrange it.
common_mistakes: Leaving a number other than 1 on the right.
Forgetting to divide one of the two terms.
